The Osa Peninsula, on Costa Rica's southern Pacific coast, is one of the most beautiful and exotic corners of the planet. Its natural environment ranks among the most biologically rich ecosystems known, with climatic and geographic conditions said to be unlike those anywhere else in Central America or the world.

Much of the peninsula is occupied by Corcovado National Park, which brings together some of Central America's largest lowland tropical forests and some of the world's highest-altitude jungles.

## Activities in Corcovado National Park

Corcovado National Park offers a wide range of activities for a rewarding escape from civilization. Visitors can watch whales and dolphins in Drake Bay, fish in coastal waters or out on the open ocean, go surfing, or rent a kayak and paddle along deserted beaches and picturesque lagoons.

Port Lockroy lies in a sheltered bay off the western coast of Wiencke Island. On nearby Goudier Island stands the British Base A, established on 11 February 1944 during Operation Tabarin. Surrounded by glaciers and snowy mountains, the buildings where polar researchers lived and carried out atmospheric studies until 1962 have been preserved.

The main building, Bransfield House, contains a museum, post office and shop. The museum presents daily life during early Antarctic expeditions, while gentoo penguins nest beside the buildings. Visits to the historic base are arranged by the expedition team; landings depend on the weather, shore conditions and permission from the station leader.

Porto Alegre is in the state of Rio Grande do Sul in southern Brazil. The city lies beside the Guaíba and is known for green neighborhoods, hilly terrain and a more temperate climate.

A city itinerary can focus on the older districts, the cathedral, the art museum and the market. Another part of the visit explores nature around the city through waterfront walks, trips into the surrounding area and green spaces.

Gaucho culture is an important part of understanding the region. An earlier Ada Tours itinerary mentions horseback riding and visits to ranches. Porto Alegre makes sense alongside Florianópolis and Curitiba on a dedicated route through southern Brazil.

Porto de Galinhas lies on the coast of Pernambuco state, south of Recife. The area's defining feature is its reefs: at low tide, natural pools form close to shore, where visitors can swim and observe marine life.

The coastline offers different experiences. Maracaípe is known for waves and surfing, while Muro Alto is sheltered by reefs and suited to a more peaceful beach break. Snorkeling, water activities and excursions along the coast can also be added to the itinerary.

Porto de Galinhas is an easy stop after Recife and Olinda. With more time available, the journey can continue from the mainland coast to Fernando de Noronha.

In the Porto Jofre area, travelers take boat trips and safaris. One of the main experiences is watching jaguars along riverbanks and areas of vegetation.

The animals move freely through the natural environment, so sightings depend on their behavior. Trips combine searching for wildlife, stops to observe animals and an introduction to the river landscapes of the northern Pantanal.
